podcast.title: Omission of Greenhouse During Search (1994)
podcast.body: During the search of Kurt Cobain's house with Detective Tom Grant, Dylan Carlson reportedly "forgot to tell Tom" about the greenhouse in the backyard. This omission meant the greenhouse, where Cobain's body was later found, was not searched that night. "Not dealing new about the greenhouse, but he apparently forgot to tell Tom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Search for Kurt Cobain (1994)
podcast.body: On the morning of April 7, 1994, Dylan Carlson, identified as Kurt Cobain's best friend, accompanied Detective Tom Grant in a search for Cobain. They checked Cobain's usual hangouts and drug dealer spots before visiting his house. "Running a car he picked up Kurt's best friend Dylan Carlson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dylan Carlson Friendship and Shotgun Purchase (March 30, 1994)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain maintained a close friendship with Dylan Carlson. On March 30, 1994, Carlson accompanied Cobain to Stan Baker's Sports in Seattle, where they purchased a Remington M11 shotgun for $308.37. Accounts differ on whether Kurt directly paid for it or if Dylan made the actual purchase after receiving money from Kurt. "He was Kurt's best friend, and he was the guy who went with Kurt to Stan Baker's Sports in Seattle, on March 30, 1994, to buy a Remington M11 shotgun for $308.37. Actually, some stories say that Kurt gave him the money, and Dylan was the person who actually bought it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: House Search Omission (1994)
xref.body: On April 7, 1994, at 2:15 AM, Detective Tom Grant and Kurt Cobain's best friend, Dylan Carlson, conducted a thorough search of Cobain's house in Seattle. Despite searching "top to bottom," they failed to check the greenhouse in the backyard, as Carlson reportedly forgot to mention its existence to Grant. "They didn't go out into the backyard to check the greenhouse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Purchase of Shotgun for "Protection" (March 30, 1994)
xref.body: On the morning he was scheduled to leave for rehab, Kurt Cobain, accompanied by his friend Dylan Carlson, visited Stan Baker's Sports, a gun store. Kurt stated he needed a new gun for protection, citing the confiscation of his previous collection by police. Carlson purchased a Rowington C-11 shotgun and a box of shells for Kurt, costing $308.17, and the weapon was taken back to the house. "Kurt had said that he needed a new gun for protection since the cops had confiscated his collection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Second Note Discovery (1994)
xref.body: The second note, allegedly found by Courtney Love, was not suicidal in nature. Instead, it purportedly stated that Kurt Cobain was leaving her and Seattle. "Kurt allegedly tells Courtney that he's leaving her and Seattle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shotgun Purchase Through a Friend (March 1994)
xref.body: On March 30, 1994, Kurt Cobain went with his friend Dylan Carlson to Stan Baker's Sports and purchased a shotgun for $303.37. The purchase was officially made by Dylan because the police had previously confiscated all of Cobain's numerous other firearms, viewing him as a threat to himself. "On March 30, he and his friend Dylan Carlson went together to stand Baker's sports where he bought a shotgun for $303.37."

xref.title: Seattle Drony Doom Band
xref.body: Earth is characterized as a "drony, doomy guitar band" hailing from Seattle, led by Dylan Carlson, who was known as Kurt Cobain's best friend. "The Drony, Do Middle Band from Seattle, headed up by Kurt Cobain's best friend Dylan Carlson, and yeah, that is Kurt singing on that track, which is called Divine and Bright."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vocals on Earth's "Divine and Bright" (Pre-Nevermind)
xref.body: Before Nirvana's "Nevermind" album was released, Kurt Cobain contributed guest vocals to the song "Divine and Bright" by the band Earth, as a favor to his friend Dylan Carlson. The recording of this song was unavailable for many years due to Carlson's struggles with addiction but was eventually reissued in 2010 on Earth's album, "A Bureaucratic Desire for Extra Capsular Extraction." "As a favor to Dylan, a pre-never-mind Kurt offered up some vocals on a song called Divine and Bright that disappeared for years because Dylan was an addict and couldn't hold it together. In 2010, a collection of recordings from that time was reissued on an album called A Bureaucratic Desire for Extra Capsular Extraction, and Divine and Bright is included."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
